text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- East Germans drug-fuelled at Games: Files of secret police show systematic steroid, hormone use at 1976 Montreal Olympics.
- Morals crimes expected to rise: Burglary rate in Canada predicted to fall.
- Family doctors poised to refuse patients: Ontario minister warns MDs of sanctions.
- U.S. election reveals his and her politics: Educated women have different agenda, study of voting patterns finds.
- Refugees trickle into aid centres: Signs hopeful that Hutu militia loosening control of camps, UN spokesman says.
- Fund fallout less than Fidelity feared.
- Fidelity, Fund manager talk severance: Two sides negotiate separation deal; fund industry's integrity 'tarnished,' observers say.
- Canadian Airlines unions reject pay cut request: 'Concessions won't save the company'
- U.K. to probe travel industry competition: Tour giants include Thomson, Airtours.
- Rogers to cut staff at cable unit: Announces cost-cutting measures after posting another loss.
- Rogers issues layoff warning as losses climb: Reports a $148 million loss that includes a $67.8 million provision to cover laying off employees and restructuring its cable operations.
- Industry critic attacks watered-down mutual fund plan.
